posts.title: Formal Automotive Security Analysis Of CAN XL  (Georgia Tech, QCRI, Purdue)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Georgia Institute of Technology, Qatar Computing Research Institute, and Purdue University published a technical paper titled “A Formal Security Analysis of CAN XL.” Abstract: “For decades, the Controller Area Network (CAN) has been the backbone of in-vehicle communication. As modern vehicles integrate cameras, LiDARs, and AI components, classic CAN (CAN CC) faces growing... » read more
The post Formal Automotive Security Analysis Of CAN XL  (Georgia Tech, QCRI, Purdue) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A formal security analysis of the next-generation CAN XL automotive communication standard revealed that it remains vulnerable to all legacy CAN CC MAC sub-layer attacks.
The researchers identified seven new vulnerabilities specific to the CAN XL architecture, which they validated through multi-stage attacks on commercial controllers.

The findings suggest that the industry's transition to CAN XL may worsen the security posture of vehicle networks unless standard revisions are formally verified and mitigated before widespread deployment.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Autonomous workflow design; CFETs push scaling beyond 10 angstroms; onsemi-Synaptics deal revised; physical AI M&A and funding; AI data centers drive new power/packaging investments; new Spectre-v2 attack targets JIT compilers; photonics moves closer to compute; quantum HW; false base station risks; 88k engineers needed.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has launched a portfolio of domain-specific AI agents and partnered with OpenAI to develop 'GPT-Synopsys,' aiming to automate multi-step engineering workflows across the entire EDA stack.
Lam Research proposed a self-aligned CFET architecture that achieves a 52.7% reduction in bit cell size compared to N3 technology, potentially enabling CMOS scaling below 10 angstroms.
South Korea reported a record $60 billion in semiconductor exports for September, a 262% year-over-year surge driven by high memory demand and pricing.
A new Spectre-v2 variant, 'Branch Target Reuse,' has been discovered targeting JIT compilers, capable of leaking sensitive data despite existing hardware mitigations.

posts.title: HBF for High-Throughput LLM Serving (UC Berkeley, FuriosaAI)
posts.summary:
Researchers at the UC Berkeley and FuriosaAI published a technical paper titled “Characterizing High Bandwidth Flash for LLM Serving.” Abstract “Large language model (LLM) serving requires substantial memory to store model weights and KV caches. As models grow larger and contexts become longer, memory capacity and bandwidth increasingly become bottlenecks for serving performance. Agentic workloads... » read more
The post HBF for High-Throughput LLM Serving (UC Berkeley, FuriosaAI) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers introduced a hierarchical storage system using High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) to address memory bottlenecks in large language model (LLM) serving, achieving completion time reductions of 36.1% to 87.0%.
The study demonstrates that buffered cache-aware scheduling is critical for HBF adoption, extending the component's write lifetime from 4.77 to 14.82 years.

While HBF offers significant energy savings of up to 55.8% for heavy workloads, the researchers noted that it can increase energy consumption for lighter tasks, necessitating careful system-level coordination.

posts.title: Tesla beats Q3 delivery expectations but falls further behind BYD in BEV sales
posts.summary:
Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles globally in the third quarter, down 2.13% year-on-year but above market expectations.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Tesla reported 486,532 global deliveries for Q3 2026, beating market expectations of 463,761 but marking a 2.13% decline year-on-year.
BYD significantly widened its lead in the battery electric vehicle (BEV) segment, selling 762,478 units in Q3 compared to Tesla's 486,532.
The gap between BYD's BEV sales and Tesla's deliveries expanded to 275,946 vehicles in Q3, up from a 76,964-unit lead in the previous quarter.
Tesla's Q3 performance ended a two-quarter streak of year-on-year growth, highlighting intensifying competition in the global EV market.
